title: Bounded width setup run
statement: For a natural parameter $K_0$, the designated machine, oracle $\mathrm{orc}:\{0,\ldots,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$, input $x$, and natural bounds $B,P$, let $q$ be one of the first-search, second-search, or final-scan phases, let $S$ be a machine state, and let $M:\mathbb Z\to\{0,1\}$ be a memory marking. Suppose $X=w=K=B_s=C=Z=0$ in $S$, $K_0>0$, every register of $S$ is at most $B$, and $3\cdot 2^{K_0(r+S.L_g+1)}\le B$, where $r$ is the radius register selected by phase $q$. Then the machine has a finite run from the copy-loop configuration for the radius of phase $q$, with state $S$, marking $M$, and memory head at zero, to the phase exit with the same marking and head position zero, and with state obtained by setting $w=K_0(r+S.L_g+1)$, $K=2^{K_0(r+S.L_g+1)}$, and $B_s=(1\text{ if }q\text{ is the second-search phase, and }2\text{ otherwise})\cdot 2^{K_0(r+S.L_g+1)}$, leaving every other state component unchanged. Every configuration strictly before the endpoint satisfies the register-instruction precondition, has all registers at most $B$, and has memory head between $0$ and $P$.

replaced:
Fix the designated machine $A(K_0)$, oracle, input, and natural bounds $B,P$. For each
phase $q$ among the first search, second search, and final scan, let $r$ be the register
selected by that phase. Suppose the registers $X,w,K,Bs,C,Z$ of a state $S$ are all
zero, $K_0>0$, every register of $S$ is at most $B$, and $3\cdot 2^{K_0(r+S.Lg+1)}\le
B$. Then the machine can run from the copy-loop configuration for that phase, with state
$S$, arbitrary memory marking, and head at zero, to the phase's exit configuration. The
final state replaces $w,K,Bs$ by $K_0(r+S.Lg+1)$, $2^{K_0(r+S.Lg+1)}$, and
$2^q2^{K_0(r+S.Lg+1)}$, respectively, where the coefficient $2^q$ is $1$ for the second
search and $2$ for either other phase; all other state components and the memory marking
and head are unchanged. Every intermediate configuration satisfies the register and head
guard: the register-instruction precondition holds, all registers are at most $B$, and
the head lies between $0$ and $P$.
